text: DSH Session Control 是面向 DeepSeek Harness Web 客户端的会话管理插件：它通过替换工作区侧栏并提供配套服务，把会话整理和归档阅读集中到 DSH 界面中。主要功能包括置顶和隐藏会话、按内容搜索、查看归档转录、批量导出 Markdown，以及用标签整理会话。它还支持空会话过滤、会话大小提示和切换目录时继续使用现有会话。适合需要管理大量 DSH 会话、查找旧对话或保存转录的用户；安装后使用宿主会话与工作区能力，模型摘要交接需另行配置 provider 和 model。

DSH Session Control adds session management to the DSH web sidebar. Pin or hide sessions, search contents, read archived transcripts, export chats as Markdown, and organize with labels. It filters blank sessions and shows size badges. Model handoff summaries need a provider and model.

如何把几个会话一起导出成 Markdown？
我想给不同项目的会话加标签分类。
侧边栏能不能隐藏空白会话和不想看的会话？
I need to find an older DSH conversation by searching its contents.
How can I export several chat transcripts as Markdown?
DSH Session Control 的功能「置顶和隐藏会话」：会话列表支持置顶常用项，也可暂时隐藏不需要显示的会话；隐藏状态可在插件设置中管理。
DSH Session Control 的功能「搜索会话」：在侧边栏输入关键词查找会话内容，并查看匹配上下文，帮助定位旧对话。
DSH Session Control 的功能「读取归档转录」：打开归档会话时，插件读取宿主保存的记录并在界面展示；支持将单条转录格式化为 Markdown。
DSH Session Control 的功能「批量导出」：选择多个会话后可生成合并的 Markdown 文档，便于保存会话记录。

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · Installation：Install via the `dsh` CLI for your web profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @goodandready/dsh-session-control
```

Restart the DeepSeek Harness web profile to activate the bundle patch.

---

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · How to Restore the Stock Sidebar：To revert to the stock sidebar at any time:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove @goodandready/dsh-session-control
```

The stock `ui-workspace` row is instantly re-enabled, returning the sidebar to its default look. All pinned and hidden session preferences are preserved in host storage and will seamlessly reapply if the plugin is installed again.

text: @goodandready/dsh-session-control README · 📌 Pinned Sessions：Pin important conversations to a dedicated, globally visible top group above workspaces. Pinned sessions survive page reloads, browser switches, and device migrations because configuration is persisted in host storage.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · 🔍 Search with Contextual Snippets：The core searches conversation contents and returns context around the matching query — `dsh-session-control` displays this preview as a second line under the session title so you immediately see why a conversation matched without opening it.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · 🗄️ Period-Based Archive：Organized into intuitive collapsible periods: *Today*, *This Week*, *This Month*, and *Older*. Collapsed periods are unmounted from the DOM, preventing performance degradation even with thousands of historical sessions. Active search automatically expands relevant periods.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · 📜 Read-Only Archived Transcript Viewer：Archived sessions cannot be opened for active chatting in the core. The plugin provides an isolated, read-only transcript viewer modal via `GET /dsh-session-control/transcript?session=<id>` to inspect past agent turns, tools called, and user prompts safely.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · 🧹 Automatic Noise Reduction (Hide Blank Sessions)：Automated schedulers, messenger gateways, and kanban boards continuously spawn sessions without messages. Blank sessions are hidden by default to keep the sidebar clean. The active session is never hidden even if empty. Toggleable via settings.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · 👁️ Reversible Session Hiding：Unlike core archiving which is one-way, `dsh-session-control` offers lightweight reversible hiding for active sessions you temporarily want out of view.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · ☑️ Multi-Select & Batch Operations：Hover checkboxes and Shift+Click range selection allow batch hiding, unhiding, and pinning of dozens of sessions simultaneously.
@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · ✏️ In-Place Inline Renaming：Rename conversations instantly with a double click on the title or by pressing `F2`.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · 🏷️ Labels：A session cannot be moved between workspaces — membership is derived from its working
directory, and the core rejects any session whose `cwd` does not match the folder path.
Labels give the grouping axis the folders cannot: assign one from the row menu or to a
whole selection at once, then filter the panel — archive included — by clicking a chip
above the list. The same menu removes it again — the entry reads *Remove from “name”*,
so the action is named, not hidden behind a checkmark. Under an active label filter the
bulk bar can strip that label from a whole selection at once. A label that loses its last
session disappears on its own.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · 🧾 Names Derived From Your First Message：Without a stored title the core shows the project folder name, so every conversation in a
folder looks the same. The plugin reads the first message you sent in that session and
uses it as the label. No model call and no cost: the text is already in the session log.
Renaming always wins — once you name a conversation, the derived label is gone. Only the
rows currently on screen are resolved, so collapsed sections cost nothing.
section: 🧾 Names Derived From Your First Message

text:
@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · ⌨️ Quick Jump (`Alt+K`)：Opens a palette over the interface that searches titles and message contents at once.
`Alt` rather than `Ctrl`: browsers keep `Ctrl+K` for themselves and never hand it to the
page. The Cyrillic layout is handled too, so the physical key works either way.
Arrows move, `Enter` opens, `Esc` closes and returns the focus where it was. An archived
result opens as a transcript, exactly as it does in the list.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · 🚦 Session Size Badges：The DSH conversation view keeps every event of a session in the page at once. In a very
large session a long agent turn can freeze the browser tab, and with it every other DSH tab
of the same site. Rows now warn before that happens: a **yellow** badge once a session is
large and a **red** one once it is dangerous for the interface. The badge shows the event
count as text, so the meaning never relies on colour alone, and its tooltip adds the log
size. Sizes come from session metadata; logs are never decompressed for this. Thresholds
default to 1 500 and 3 000 events and can be changed in the settings card.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · ↪️ Continue in a New Session：From a row's menu, **Continue in new session** opens a new chat in the same workspace and
places a **draft** into its composer: the previous session's name and workspace, your recent
requests and the agent's last report. Nothing is sent — you read, edit and send it yourself.
The extract is assembled instantly and needs no model.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · ↪️ Continue in a New Session：**Continue with a model summary** does the same with a model-written summary instead: goal,
what is done, what is open, agreements and key references. It spends model tokens, so it
runs only on an explicit click and stays disabled until a provider and model are set in the
settings card. A very large session is not handed to the model whole: the newest part within
the configured budget is used, and the summary says so.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · 📤 Markdown Export：The transcript window can copy the conversation to the clipboard or save it as a `.md`
file. A truncated transcript says so in the export itself, so a fragment is never mistaken
for the whole conversation.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · Intentional Constraints：* **No cross-workspace session moving:** Workspaces represent distinct disk directories. Session membership is derived directly from the session's working directory (`cwd`). The core registry strictly enforces this binding.
* **No unarchiving:** DeepSeek Harness core provides an archive operation but no unarchive API method. Archived sessions remain accessible via the read-only transcript viewer.
* **Legacy log format handling:** Older legacy session logs that cannot be deserialized by the core are gracefully flagged with descriptive notices rather than displaying a false "no messages" state.
* **No session hard deletion:** Session deletion is not exposed in public harness APIs, and the plugin adheres strictly to safe API contracts.
@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · HTTP API Routes Reference：The host half of the plugin exposes three dedicated endpoints via Cordis `webServer`:

| `GET` | `/dsh-session-control/titles` | `sessions=<id1,id2,...>` | JSON `{"ok": true, "titles": { "<id>": "<title>" }}` | Infers conversational preview titles from the user's first prompt (up to 60 IDs per batch; cached in host process memory). |

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · Architecture & Reliability：The plugin utilizes a decoupled **two-half architecture** for maximum resilience:

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · Architecture & Reliability：1. **Service Half (`uiWorkspace` Provider):**
   * The replaced core `ui-workspace` module exports a required service `uiWorkspace` that is an essential dependency for `dsh-client-ui-sidebar` and `dsh-client-ui-conversation`.
   * The plugin's service half delivers this service and root hooks cleanly with zero React rendering and zero plugin logic overhead.
2. **Interface Half (UI & Views):**
   * Encapsulates the custom workspace tree, search results, transcript modal, and settings card.
   * Completely wrapped in defensive error boundaries. If a UI exception occurs, the main sidebar, conversation pane, and settings remain fully operational.
3. **Server Route:**
   * Exposes `GET /dsh-session-control/transcript` to parse and stream archived JSONL session logs safely without loading heavy unneeded payloads.

@goodandready/dsh-session-control README · UI Localization：The plugin core ships with English strings by default. Multilingual localizations (including Russian and Chinese) are loaded through language packs (such as `@goodandready/dsh-russian-lang`). Dictionary registration is fail-safe and never degrades sidebar functionality.
